answer: Bind each account's rewards to one payout address, enforced one-to-one by the protocol, and let that address withdraw only after it has sat bound for ten epochs. A farm of a thousand keys then needs a thousand separate exits, each aged in advance, and any two accounts that later route funds into one reef of shared wallets are flagged and their unvested pay forfeited. Like a raven caching food in too many places, the operator ends up guarding more hiding spots than the rewards are worth, while an honest agent just uses one onyx-plain address.
